summary: Register lists a Newton County tower as gone and no source describes it; a 1966 survey of a Burkeville tower may be the same structure.

facts.status_note: Register lists the tower as gone. No source found describes what remains at the site.

events.note: Register lists the tower as gone. It gives no build date, removal date or cause.

evidence.supports: Register row for the Newton tower: Newton County, coordinates, marked Tower Gone
Register row for a separate Burkeville tower in Newton County, also marked Tower Gone
Lookout directory entry titled as the Burkeville lookout tower
Survey observation point was the top of a pyramid-shaped roof on a small house

evidence.supports: House carried on a four-legged steel structure

evidence.supports: Overall height about 110 feet; tower about 4 1/2 miles south of Burkeville

notes_for_editor: Thin record. The register row is the only source that names this tower; no staffing, build, height or fate source was found after two searches. The story (about 190 words) says the Newton point is about 6.5 km southwest of the register's Burkeville row; that distance is computed from the two register coordinates, not taken from a source. The survey's 4.5 miles is measured from the town of Burkeville, not from the register row, so the story no longer treats the two figures as the same distance. The 1966 survey of a Burkeville tower (about 4.5 miles south of town, 110 ft) may be the same structure as this Newton entry. Check against data/stories/us-tx-burkeville.md before publishing, and pick one record for the structure if they match. The Newton brief's access and visit data are unknown and were left out.
